The State has filed this writ appeal challenging the direction issued by the learned Single Judge,
whereby the Competent Authority for Land Acquisition (CALA) under the National Highway Act was directed to pass orders on Ext.P4.
The writ petitioners had specifically contended that they were entitled to compensation for the unacquired portion of their land on account of injurious affection.
Their prayer was either for acquisition of the remaining unacquired land or in the alternative, for payment of compensation for the injurious affection caused to it.
2. It is now reported by the learned Government Pleader that the award has already been passed.
If the petitioners have any further claim for compensation, the Court cannot compel the National Highways Authority or the State to acquire the remaining unacquired portion of the land.
3. The learned Single Judge referred to Section 94 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ('RFCTLARR Act').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Though, in principle, that provision may not apply in view of the order of the WA NO. 2713 OF 2025 District Collector vs Jacob Thomas on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187340713/
2 4 2025:KER:93304 Division Bench produced as Annexure 1, nevertheless no impediment in computing compensation for the unacquired portion of the land in terms of Section 3G(7) of the National Highways Act, 2013 r/w Section 28 of the RFCTLARR Act.
That be the case, the remedy of the writ petitioners is to invoke arbitration remedy against the award.
We reserve liberty to the writ petitioners to pursue the arbitration remedy for claiming compensation in respect of the unacquired land.

Accordingly, this writ appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment is set aside, leaving it open to the writ petitioners to seek compensation through arbitration in the light of the interim order marked as Annexure 1 and the judgment marked as Annexure 2.
Sd/-
